components.note: 讠 (speech) — mistakes of words or judgment
吴 (wú) gives the sound — a near match for wù

example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, zhè shì yí ge wùhuì.
example.english: Sorry, this is a misunderstanding.
example.fact: 误 is a mistake or a harmful delay: 误会 (misunderstanding, the most common word), 错误 (error), 耽误 (to hold up), 误解, 失误 (a slip), 误导 (to mislead). It sounds more formal than 错.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the body of a person
建 (jiàn) gives the sound — it matches exactly and also suggests "building up"

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān qù jiànshēnfáng duànliàn.
example.english: She works out at the gym every day.
example.fact: 健 means strong and healthy, and it is mostly in compounds: 健康 (health), 健身 (to work out), 健全 (sound, complete), 健谈 (talkative), 保健品 (health supplements).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — leaning against or moving close
矣 (yǐ) gives only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā āi zhe wǒ zuò zài hòupái.
example.english: He sat next to me in the back row.
example.fact: 挨 has two readings. āi means "next to" or "in turn": 挨着, 挨家挨户 (door to door), 挨个 (one by one). ái means "to suffer": 挨骂 (to be scolded), 挨饿 (to go hungry), 挨打. Context picks the reading.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a guest is received under a roof
兵 (bīng) replaces the old gift-bearing part in simplification and gives a rough sound

example.pinyin: Huānyíng gèwèi láibīn.
example.english: Welcome, all guests.
example.fact: 宾 means guest: 来宾, 外宾 (foreign guest), 嘉宾 (honored guest on a show), 宾馆 (a hotel). In grammar, 宾语 is the object of a sentence, treated as the "guest" of the verb.

components.note: 车 (cart) — the original sense relates to carts
交 (jiāo) gives the sound — close to jiào

example.hanzi: 这家店的东西比较便宜。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi bǐjiào piányi.
example.english: The things at this shop are relatively cheap.
example.fact: 较 means "to compare" or "relatively." 比较 can be a verb (to compare) or an adverb (fairly). 较真 means taking something too seriously, 计较 is to haggle over small things, and 较量 means to compete.

components.note: A picture of swirling clouds; the character was later given a rain top (雲) and the simple form revived in simplification

example.pinyin: Tiānshàng yǒu hěn duō báiyún.
example.english: There are many white clouds in the sky.
example.fact: Clouds are counted with 朵: 一朵云. Online, 云 has become a tech word: 云计算 (cloud computing), 云端 (the cloud). In classical Chinese 云 meant "to say," as in 人云亦云 (to just parrot what others say).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — holding something in the mouth
今 (jīn) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Zhège tāng lǐ hán yǒu hěn duō yán.
example.english: This soup contains a lot of salt.
example.fact: 含 is to hold or contain: 含量 (content), 包含, 含糖 (contains sugar, seen on labels), 含羞 (shy). 含蓄 means subtle or implicit, often used for the Chinese communication style.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — stopping something with the hands
兰 (lán) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.hanzi: 他在路边拦了一辆出租车。
example.pinyin: Tā zài lùbiān lán le yí liàng chūzūchē.
example.english: He flagged down a taxi at the roadside.
example.fact: 拦 is to put your arm in the way: 拦车 (to flag down a car), 拦住 (to stop), 阻拦 (to obstruct), 拦截 (to intercept). 拦路虎, a "tiger blocking the road," is a metaphor for an obstacle.

components.note: 纟 (silk) — ropes were originally twisted from fibers
黾 (mǐn) gives only a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 他用绳子把箱子绑起来。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng shéngzi bǎ xiāngzi bǎng qǐlái.
example.english: He tied the box up with a rope.
example.fact: 绳 is usually 绳子, counted with 根 or 条. 跳绳 (jumping rope) is a common school sport, and 绳之以法 means to bring someone to justice, literally "to bind with the rope of the law."

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — a bird being roasted
灬 (fire) — the flame beneath it

example.pinyin: Miànbāo kǎo jiāo le.
example.english: The bread got burnt.
example.fact: 焦 is burnt: 焦糖 (caramel), 烤焦. By extension it describes burning worry: 焦虑 (anxiety), 焦急 (anxious). 焦点 (focus) and 焦距 (focal length) come from the same idea of a focal point.

components.note: A form with a head-like 自 above and a foot 夂 below; how it came to mean "summer" is not clear

example.hanzi: 夏天太热了，我想去海边。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān tài rè le, wǒ xiǎng qù hǎibiān.
example.english: Summer is too hot, I want to go to the seaside.
example.fact: 夏 is also an old name for China: 华夏 and the Xia dynasty, traditionally the first dynasty. Related: 夏令营 (summer camp) and 夏至 (the summer solstice, one of the 24 solar terms).

components.note: 讠 (speech) — discussing with words
仑 (lún) gives the sound — close to lùn

example.hanzi: 我们来讨论一下这个问题。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen lái tǎolùn yíxià zhège wèntí.
example.english: Let's discuss this question.
example.fact: 论 builds 讨论 (to discuss), 理论 (theory), 论文 (a thesis or paper), 结论 (conclusion) and 无论 (no matter what). 论斤卖 means selling by weight.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — paying back or losing money
咅 (pǒu) gives only a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 你打坏了我的杯子，要赔我。
example.pinyin: Nǐ dǎhuài le wǒ de bēizi, yào péi wǒ.
example.english: You broke my cup, so you should pay me back.
example.fact: 赔 is about money: 赔钱 (to lose money), 赔偿 (to compensate), 赔礼道歉 (to apologize with a gift). It is a homophone of 陪 (péi, to accompany); the 贝 radical points to money.

components.note: 水 (water) — traditionally explained as a long, flowing stream, something that does not end

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn bú huì wàngjì nǐ.
example.english: I will never forget you.
example.fact: 永 gives 永远 (forever), 永久 (permanent), 永恒 (eternal), 永不 (never). In calligraphy, 永 is famous as the character that contains all eight basic brush strokes, practiced in the 永字八法.

components.note: 女 (woman) — makeup and adornment were traditionally women's matters
丬 gives a loose sound hint, as in 状 and 壮

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang huà zhuāng.
example.english: She puts on makeup every morning.
example.fact: 妆 builds 化妆 (to put on makeup), 化妆品 (cosmetics), 卸妆 (to remove makeup), 淡妆 / 浓妆 (light/heavy makeup) and 嫁妆 (a bride's trousseau).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — stirring is done by hand
觉 (jué) gives only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ kāfēi jiǎo yi jiǎo.
example.english: Please stir the coffee.
example.fact: 搅 means to stir: 搅拌 (to mix), 搅拌机 (a blender). It also means to disturb: 打搅 ("sorry to disturb you"), 搅乱 (to mess up), 搅局 (to spoil the occasion).

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — traditionally linked to wounds from arrows, which the first medicine treated
匸 (container) — an enclosed box, like a quiver, around the arrow

example.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng yīshēng.
example.english: She is a doctor.
example.fact: 医 builds 医生 (doctor), 医院 (hospital), 医药 (medicine), 看医生 (to see a doctor). The traditional form 醫 also has 酉 (alcohol), since wine was used as medicine; the simplified form dropped it.

components.note: 言 (speech) — an oath is spoken
折 (zhé) gives only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā fāshì yǒngyuǎn ài tā.
example.english: He swore to love her forever.
example.fact: 誓 is a solemn vow: 发誓 (to swear), 誓言 (a pledge), 宣誓 (to take an oath), 誓不罢休 (to vow not to stop). 我发誓 ("I swear") is also used lightly in conversation.

components.note: 土 (earth) — filling up the ground to support
执 (zhí) gives only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Yǐzi shàng yǒu yí ge ruǎndiàn.
example.english: There is a soft cushion on the chair.
example.fact: 垫 means a pad: 垫子, 鼠标垫 (mouse pad). As a verb it means to pad or prop up, and in daily speech 垫钱 / 垫付 means to pay in advance for someone and be reimbursed later. 垫底 means to finish last.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a bay is a curve of water
弯 (wān) gives the sound and meaning — it is the curved shape, and is exactly the same sound

example.pinyin: Zhège hǎiwān hěn piàoliang.
example.english: This bay is very beautiful.
example.fact: 湾 is a bay: 海湾, 港湾. 台湾 (Taiwan) literally means "terrace bay." 湾区 means a bay area, and 粤港澳大湾区 is the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area.

components.note: 纟 (silk) — a fine thread
田 (tián) replaces the old part 囟 (xìn) in simplification, as a rough sound stand-in

example.pinyin: Zhè gēn xiàn hěn xì.
example.english: This thread is very thin.
example.fact: 细 is the opposite of 粗 and describes thin round things like thread or legs; flat things like paper use 薄. It also means careful and detailed: 仔细, 细心, 细节 (detail), 细菌 (bacteria).

components.note: 心 (heart) — a stifled feeling inside
门 (mén) gives the sound — close to mēn, and the door frame suggests being shut in

example.pinyin: Wū lǐ tài mēn le, kāi chuāng ba.
example.english: It is stuffy in the room, so open the window.
example.fact: 闷 has two readings: mēn is physically stuffy (闷热 muggy, 闷在家里 stuck at home), and mèn is a gloomy feeling (烦闷, 郁闷 depressed). Colloquially, 闷得慌 means "bored or oppressed."

components.note: 饣 (food) — the original sense is abundance of food
尧 (yáo) gives the sound — close to ráo

example.pinyin: Zhè cì ráo le nǐ, xià cì bù xíng.
example.english: I'll let you off this time, but not next time.
example.fact: 饶 means to spare or forgive: 饶恕, 求饶 (to beg for mercy), 饶命 (spare my life). In shops it can mean to add something free: 饶你一个. 富饶 means rich and abundant, and 饶舌 is the Chinese term for rap music.

components.note: 心 (heart) — fear is a feeling
巩 (gǒng) gives the sound — close to kǒng

example.pinyin: Tā kǒngpà bú huì lái le.
example.english: I'm afraid he won't be coming.
example.fact: 恐 is fear: 恐惧, 恐怖 (terror), 恐龙 (dinosaur, "terrifying dragon"). 恐怕 can mean "I'm afraid that," a polite way to deliver a likely negative outcome.

components.note: 王 (jade) — gems and precious stones
白 (bái) gives a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 这块琥珀里有一只小虫。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài hǔpò lǐ yǒu yì zhī xiǎo chóng.
example.english: There is a small insect in this piece of amber.
example.fact: 珀 exists only inside 琥珀 (amber). An old folk explanation says amber was the soul of a tiger turned to stone (虎魄), which is why the first character looks like 虎.

excludeSuggestion: Bound character found only in 琥珀 (amber).

components.note: 木 (tree) — a plum is a tree
每 (měi) gives the sound — a near match for méi

example.pinyin: Dōngtiān méihuā kāi le.
example.english: The plum blossoms bloom in winter.
example.fact: 梅 flowers in cold weather, making plum blossom a symbol of resilience. It belongs to the "Four Gentlemen" of art (梅兰竹菊: plum, orchid, bamboo, chrysanthemum). 梅雨 is the early-summer rainy season.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, in the sense of a nation
我 (wǒ) gives only a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 他会说俄语，也会说英语。
example.pinyin: Tā huì shuō Éyǔ, yě huì shuō Yīngyǔ.
example.english: He speaks Russian and English.
example.fact: 俄 is short for 俄罗斯 (Russia), a transliteration of Rossiya: 俄语, 俄国. In classical Chinese it also meant "suddenly," as in 俄而.

components.note: A simplified form of 專; the strokes no longer show a clear picture

example.pinyin: Tā shì zhè fāngmiàn de zhuānjiā.
example.english: He is an expert in this area.
example.fact: 专 means focused on one thing: 专业 (major, profession), 专家 (expert), 专心 (to concentrate), 专门 (specifically), 专利 (patent). 专车 is also a ride-hailing service.

components.note: 氵 (water) — pouring water
雚 (guàn) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Nóngmín zài gěi tiándì guàn shuǐ.
example.english: The farmers are irrigating the fields.
example.fact: 灌 builds 灌溉 (irrigation) and 灌输 (to instill). On forums, 灌水 means to post filler. 灌饼 is a Chinese breakfast flatbread filled with egg, and 灌篮 is a basketball slam dunk.

components.note: 氵 (water) — adding more liquid, like refilling a cup
忝 (tiǎn) gives the sound — close to tiān

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài gěi wǒ tiān yì wǎn fàn.
example.english: Please give me another bowl of rice.
example.fact: 添 means to add or refill: 添饭, 添加 (to add), 增添. 添麻烦 (to cause trouble) is a staple of politeness: 给您添麻烦了, "sorry for the trouble."

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a transcribed foreign sound
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān pǎo wǔ lǐ.
example.english: He runs five miles every day.
example.fact: 哩 was an old transliteration of "mile," now replaced by 英里 in the standard language. The same character is also a dialect particle, as in 好着哩, used for emphasis.

excludeSuggestion: Old or variant written form for "mile" (standard: 英里); also a dialect particle.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — cookware is made of metal
呙 (guō) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Māma yòng guō zhǔ tāng.
example.english: Mom is cooking soup in the pot.
example.fact: 锅 covers pots and woks: 炒锅 (wok), 火锅 (hot pot), 电饭锅 (rice cooker), 压力锅. In slang, 背锅 means to take the blame, literally "carry the pot," and 甩锅 means to shift it onto someone else.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the original sense was planting and growing
乙 (yǐ) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā yǒu yì mén hǎo shǒuyì.
example.english: He has a good craft skill.
example.fact: 艺 originally meant planting, which is why it has the grass radical, and later grew to "skill." It builds 艺术 (art), 手艺 (craftsmanship), 才艺 (talent), 园艺 (gardening) and 工艺 (craft).

components.note: 石 (stone) — the sound of something hard hitting
平 (píng) gives the sound — a loose match for pēng

example.pinyin: Mén pēng de yì shēng guān shàng le.
example.english: The door shut with a bang.
example.fact: 砰 imitates a loud bang. 砰的一声 means "with a bang." 砰砰 can also describe a heart pounding: 心砰砰跳. Compare 乒乓 (pīngpāng), the sound of table tennis.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a pit dug in the ground
亢 (kàng) gives the sound — close to kēng

example.pinyin: Lù shàng yǒu yí ge hěn dà de kēng.
example.english: There is a huge pit in the road.
example.fact: 坑 is a hole: 水坑 (puddle), 坑洼 (bumpy). It is slang for a scam: 被坑了 (got ripped off), 坑人 (to cheat people). 萝卜坑, a "radish hole," describes a position that is already taken.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking to a superior
王 (king) — the person addressed; the dictionary reads it as speaking before a king

example.hanzi: 湖水呈现出美丽的蓝色。
example.pinyin: Húshuǐ chéngxiàn chū měilì de lánsè.
example.english: The lake appears a beautiful blue.
example.fact: 呈 means to present or to appear in a form: 呈现 (to show), 呈上 (to hand up), 呈报 (to report to a superior). 呈 plus a shape or color describes appearance, as in 呈圆形 (round in shape).

components.note: ⺼ (meat) — animal glue was boiled from hides and tissue
交 (jiāo) gives the sound — it matches exactly and suggests joining

example.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yì guǎn jiāoshuǐ.
example.english: I need a tube of glue.
example.fact: 胶 is anything gluey or rubbery: 胶水, 胶带 (tape), 橡胶 (rubber), 胶囊 (capsule), 胶卷 (film). 阿胶 is a traditional Chinese medicine made from donkey hide.

components.note: A hooked shape: 勹 wrapped around 厶, suggesting something bent or caught

example.hanzi: 请在正确的答案上打勾。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèngquè de dá'àn shàng dǎ gōu.
example.english: Please put a tick next to the correct answer.
example.fact: 勾 is a hook: 打勾 (to tick), 勾结 (to collude), 勾引 (to lure), 勾画 (to outline). In geometry, 勾股定理 is the Pythagorean theorem, and 勾 is also read gòu in 勾当 (a shady deal).

components.note: 亻 (person) — urging someone
崔 (cuī) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.hanzi: 妈妈一直催我早点睡觉。
example.pinyin: Māma yìzhí cuī wǒ zǎodiǎn shuìjiào.
example.english: Mom keeps urging me to go to bed early.
example.fact: 催 means to hurry someone: 催促, 催债 (to press for a debt), 催眠 (to hypnotize), 催泪弹 (tear gas). 催婚, being pressured by family to get married, is a familiar social phenomenon at Spring Festival.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — an odd habit as a kind of ailment
辟 (pì) gives the sound — close to pǐ

example.pinyin: Tā yǒu shōují shǒubiǎo de pǐhào.
example.english: He has a passion for collecting watches.
example.fact: 癖 is a strong habit or fixation: 癖好 (a hobby one is attached to), 怪癖 (a quirk), 洁癖 (obsessive cleanliness, a common self-description). The sick radical suggests it was once seen as a minor ailment.

components.note: 阝 (mound) — the shady side of a hill
月 (moon) — the dictionary reads it as the moon's place; the dark, cool side

example.hanzi: 今天是阴天，可能会下雨。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān shì yīntiān, kěnéng huì xià yǔ.
example.english: Today is overcast and it might rain.
example.fact: 阴 is the shady side, as opposed to 阳 (sunny side). It is the 阴 of 阴阳 (yin and yang), and it extends to negative senses: 阴险 (sinister), 阴谋 (conspiracy). 阴历 is the lunar calendar.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — counting sticks were made of bamboo
寿 (shòu) gives only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tāmen zhèngzài chóu qián bàn xuéxiào.
example.english: They are raising money to open a school.
example.fact: 筹 was a bamboo counting stick, and from counting came planning: 筹备 (to prepare), 筹款 (to raise funds), 众筹 (crowdfunding), 统筹 (overall planning). 稍逊一筹 means "slightly inferior."

components.note: 礻 (altar) — it was originally an altar for the earth god
土 (earth) — the earth god worshiped there

example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā chūbǎnshè gōngzuò.
example.english: He works at a publishing house.
example.fact: 社 began as an altar to the god of the land. 社稷 (altars of earth and grain) stood for the state. Now it is 社会 (society), 社区 (community), 社交 (social life), 报社 (newspaper) and 旅行社 (travel agency).

components.note: 虫 (insect) — honey is made by bees
宓 (mì) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài chá lǐ jiā fēngmì.
example.english: I like to add honey to my tea.
example.fact: 蜜 is honey: 蜂蜜. A bee is 蜜蜂 (honey bee), the same two characters in the other order. 蜜月 is honeymoon, and 甜蜜 describes sweetness in a relationship; 蜜饯 is candied fruit.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — a thicket of grass, the old sense
溥 (pǔ) gives a rough sound hint

example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn báo.
example.english: This book is very thin.
example.fact: 薄 is the opposite of 厚 and describes flat things such as books or clothes. In compounds it is read bó, as in 薄弱 (weak), 淡薄 (faint), 刻薄 (mean). 薄荷 (mint) is read bòhe.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — bells are made of metal
令 (lìng) gives the sound — close to líng

example.pinyin: Xiàkè líng xiǎng le.
example.english: The bell for the end of class rang.
example.fact: 铃 is a small bell: 门铃 (doorbell), 铃声 (ringtone or bell sound), 车铃 (bicycle bell), 哑铃 (dumbbell, literally "mute bell"). In Japanese names, 铃木 is Suzuki.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — taxes were once paid in grain
兑 (duì) gives only a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Nǐ yào jiāo duōshao shuì?
example.english: How much tax do you have to pay?
example.fact: 税 is tax: 交税 (to pay tax), 个人所得税 (personal income tax, shortened to 个税), 关税 (customs duty), 免税 (duty-free), 增值税 (VAT).

components.note: 禾 (grain) — originally tied to measuring grain and standards
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.hanzi: 我们先看一下今天的行程。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān kàn yíxià jīntiān de xíngchéng.
example.english: Let's first look at today's itinerary.
example.fact: 程 started as a measure or standard and extended to a stage of a journey or process: 行程 (itinerary), 路程 (distance), 过程 (process), 课程 (course), 工程 (engineering project), 程序 (program), 程序员 (programmer).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pinching is done with the fingers
圼 (niè) gives the sound — close to niē

example.pinyin: Tā niē le niē wǒ de shǒu.
example.english: She gave my hand a squeeze.
example.fact: 捏 is to pinch or to shape with the fingers: 捏饺子 (to crimp dumplings), 捏泥人 (to make clay figures), 捏造 (to fabricate). 捏一把汗 means to be anxious for someone, "pinching a handful of sweat."

components.note: A simplified form of 衛; the strokes no longer show a clear picture

example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, wèishēngjiān zài nǎlǐ?
example.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
example.fact: 卫 means to guard: 保卫, 自卫, 卫士 (guard). 卫生 is hygiene, and 卫生间 is the polite word for a restroom. 卫星 (satellite) is literally a "guard star."
